core_findings: Tamarac is a real incorporated municipality. The City's official history page says Tamarac was incorporated on July 19, 1963.

As of March 24, 2026, Tamarac's current primary general-policing entity is Broward Sheriff's Office, not a city-run Tamarac Police Department. Tamarac's official volunteer page says BSO provides police services for the City of Tamarac, and BSO's official Tamarac district page lists a Tamarac law-enforcement office at 7515 Pine Island Road.

The contract-policing structure is longstanding. In the City's official September 23, 2020 commission meeting transcript, Tamarac approved a police-services agreement with BSO effective October 1, 2020 through September 30, 2025 with one five-year renewal option, and city staff described it as a continuation of BSO agreements that had been in place for over the last twenty five years.

Florida's official county-and-municipal offense publications support a real Tamarac-specific annual reporting identity through the transition period. FDLE's 2020 report lists Tamarac Police Department with population 66,089 and total index crime 1,155, and FDLE's 2021 report retains Tamarac Police Department as a named Broward municipal row with population 72,509 even though every offense cell is blank.

Florida's post-SRS public offense workbook no longer publishes Tamarac. Inspection of FDLE's official FIBRS Offense Detail 2021-2025 Q2 workbook found no Tamarac Police Department row in the 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, or 2025 Q2 sheets.

The FBI Crime Data Explorer agency roster still carries Tamarac's legacy agency identity. The official CDE Florida agency endpoint lists Tamarac Police Department in Broward County under ORI FL0063100, but marks is_nibrs as false and nibrs_start_date as null.

Repo evidence matches a continuity collapse under a contract-city model rather than a bad municipal target. The live crosswalk routes FL0063100 exclusively to Tamarac city, agency_master classifies FL0063100 as a local police department with SRS and NIBRS source-presence flags through 2024, and agency_year_observations shows positive annual totals in 2018, 2019, and 2020 before zero rows from 2021 through 2024. jurisdiction_controls_2024 then fully fills every 2024 Tamarac offense row from historical medians.

why: Tamarac is a valid incorporated municipality.
Current city and sheriff sources show Tamarac is still a distinct city-specific policing object even though operations are delivered by BSO under contract.
FDLE officially published Tamarac Police Department as a municipal row with substantive 2020 counts and retained the Tamarac row in 2021.
The FBI CDE roster still carries Tamarac Police Department as a Florida city agency tied to FL0063100, even though it is not marked as a NIBRS participant.
The live repo crosswalk from FL0063100 to Tamarac city matches that historical Tamarac-specific reporting identity.
likely_explanation_for_current_all_fill_: Tamarac's legacy municipal reporting identity survived administratively into the 2021 transition but lost public offense continuity after the SRS-era county-and-municipal report path.

The contract-city structure made the legacy city row fragile during the SRS-to-NIBRS transition: FDLE kept Tamarac as a blank row in 2021, the public FIBRS workbook stopped publishing it, and FBI CDE does not show Tamarac as a NIBRS agency.

Because FL0063100 remained exclusively attached to Tamarac in reference while official post-2020 offense continuity vanished, the 2024 control builder treated the city as structurally missing and fully filled it.

best_available_override_surface_if_busin.source: Tamarac-specific BSO district records or city-held contract-performance materials
best_available_override_surface_if_busin.why: The current public FDLE and FBI surfaces do not provide post-2020 Tamarac offense counts, but Tamarac still has a distinct BSO district and city-managed police-services contract structure.
limitations: No ready-made official public annual offense table for Tamarac after 2020 was found in the reviewed materials.
A later override would require direct Tamarac-district BSO records, city public-records retrieval, or other city-held contract reporting outputs.

recommended_handling: Retain Tamarac city as a standalone municipal control row.
Document Tamarac explicitly as a BSO contract-policing municipality rather than treating it as a standard city-run police department.
Do not drop Tamarac into generic Broward County nonmunicipal remainder.
Treat the current full-fill state as a reporting continuity and publication failure on FL0063100 under a contract-city municipal reporting model.
Use FDLE's county-and-municipal offense reports as the official state truth surface through 2021, with 2020 as the last substantive annual offense row.

open_questions: The keep versus drop decision is closed. The remaining implementation blocker is that no reviewed official public source exposes ready-made post-2020 Tamarac offense totals; any later override would need Tamarac-specific BSO district records or city-held contract-reporting material.
